page.layout: One column of verse, centred on the page, with the author's name set right-aligned below it; below that a centred small heading "Ad eundem.", then a second verse poem with a drop-cap initial, and a right-aligned signature at the foot. No margin notes, running head or page number.

main_text.p: Arduamagnarum ponis festigia rerum, Laudata Astraea discutienda choro. Nomina sicscriptis ornant, famamq; perennem, Est quibus ad summum tendere cura gradum. Macte hoc tali ausu, non parua exempla secute: Et metam fausto sidere latus adi. Tempus erit, quo te Iurisprudentia alumno Gaudeat, & laudes tollat ad astra tuas. Tunc me si veteres inter numerabis amicos, Ingenio quanquam clarus & arte magis: Experiere animum plenum candore; tibiq; Firma seruabis pectora nostra fide. Interea facilis superent tibi tempora vitae: Duret & ingenij judicijq; vigor.
main_text.head: Ad eundem.
main_text.p: ET LE[?]TERSPERGERE tibi Themis inclita seruat Labore dignam adoream. Tramite legitimo dubias decidere lites Lex postulat. Sed judicum In diuersa tamen non nemo videtur abire. Obnubilante candidum VERUM errore, animum aut fallente cupidine dire Pellacis auri, hos tu doces Evitare dolos: causamq; examine monstras Novo excuti sincerius. Iustitia exultat sic tandem lege ministra: Et sunt bonorum praemia Certa: malosq; premit poenae gravis exitus: atte[?] Manet perennis gloria.

page.notes: The first word of the second poem, printed as "ET LEITERSPERGERE" with the second and third letters overlapping, is uncertain; the reading "LE[?]TERSPERGERE" is a best guess. The word ending "atte" at the end of the line before "Manet" carries a tail mark that could not be resolved. The final word "dire" has a doubtful final letter. Line breaks within each verse stanza are kept. The drop-cap E is joined to "ET". No page number or running head is printed.
